title: Double anticrossings induced by nonlinear magnon interactions
authors: Geil Emdi, Tomosato Hioki, Koujiro Hoshi, Takahiko Makiuchi, Aoi Yamauchi, Eiji Saitoh
abstract: We observe pump-induced double anticrossings whose gap sizes and center-frequency shifts depend strongly on pump power, indicating a nonlinear mechanism. The anticrossings vanish at high magnetic fields, where energy conservation suppresses three-magnon splitting, thereby identifying the underlying process as three-magnon scattering. We attribute the double anticrossings to nondegenerate three-magnon splitting, which generates two magnon populations at distinct frequencies. Each population forms a standing-wave mode and couples independently to the Kittel mode, giving rise to two effective coupling channels. These results demonstrate that nonlinear magnon interactions can dynamically generate multiple coupling channels within a single system.
summary: This work investigates how strong, nonlinear magnon interactions in patterned magnetic films can spontaneously create multiple distinct energy coupling pathways. By observing and modeling double anticrossings whose characteristics depend strongly on pump power, the authors prove that three-magnon scattering generates two separate magnon populations, effectively creating multiple independent coupling channels within one physical system.
main_problem: To demonstrate that nonlinear magnon interactions can dynamically generate multiple emergent coupling channels within a single magnetic system, moving beyond channels fixed by device geometry.
main_result: The system exhibits pump-induced double anticrossings attributed to nondegenerate three-magnon splitting, which generates two distinct magnon populations and thus two effective coupling channels with the Kittel mode.
method: A combination of microwave spectroscopy (VNA measurements) on patterned permalloy films and theoretical modeling using a three-magnon coupling Hamiltonian ($	ext{H}_{	ext{nd}}$) coupled to an effective mean-field interaction ($	ext{H}_{	ext{c,eff}}$).
model_or_system: The physical system is spin waves (magnons) in patterned permalloy films. The model involves three-magnon scattering processes and the coupling of the resulting secondary magnon pairs to a primary Kittel mode.
key_observables: Double anticrossing features in the $S_{21}$ spectrum, frequency gap ($\Delta f_{	ext{gap}}$), and central frequency shift ($\delta\omega_c$).
important_parameters: Pump power ($P$), applied magnetic field ($B$), and wavevector ($k$). The dependence of observables on $P$ confirms nonlinearity.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on developing an effective coupling Hamiltonian in the mean-field approximation after deriving the three-magnon interaction terms.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic dispersion, initial single dip splitting into two dips upon pumping, and the evolution of a double anticrossing feature as the magnetic field increases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental observation (single/double anticrossings dependent on pump power) to theoretical interpretation, attributing the features to nondegenerate three-magnon splitting which creates multiple coupling channels. The analysis confirms predictions based on derived Hamiltonians and scaling laws for gap size and frequency shift.
why_interesting: The ability to dynamically generate multiple coupling channels via nonlinear magnon interactions is highly relevant to understanding engineered quantum systems where mode coupling dictates device functionality, bridging concepts from cavity QED/optomechanics into magnonics.
